deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 15% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 75% last year; 22%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $131M, down 92% from a year ago — about 3% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $58M, up 33% from a year ago.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $32 of operating profit, up from $18 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Only 75% of reported profit became spare cash, usually because of heavy investment; worth watching.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 28× last year's profit (lower than 53% of the last 5 years).
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.
